key_insight: The paper introduces new MRS-based optimization methods that efficiently find multiple statistical equilibria of 2D turbulent flows on a sphere while preserving all Casimir invariants.
engineering_relevance: These methods improve practical prediction of geophysical flow end states, including symmetry-broken vortex patterns relevant to atmospheric and oceanic modeling.
method: Two canonical solvers for mixing-entropy maximization under MRS theory
One microcanonical solver that retains all conserved quantities
Designed to better detect multiple equilibria and non-zonal solutions
evidence_signal: Applied to a barotropically unstable zonal vorticity distribution, the methods found two equilibria: a zonal wavenumber-1 state and a wavenumber-2 state, with the former maximizing mixing entropy.
watch_item: Because the approach targets idealized statistical equilibria on spherical geometry, careful numerical setup is needed to avoid missing metastable branches or over-interpreting agreement with time integration.
paper_title: New numerical methods for calculating statistical equilibria of two-dimensional turbulent flows, strictly based on the Miller-Robert-Sommeria theory
